strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation across 4 diverse tasks (retrieval, VQA, reasoning, classification) with multiple datasets and backbone models demonstrating consistent improvements
Significant practical efficiency gains (43.3× speedup, 23.9× cost reduction) addressing a major bottleneck in existing graph-based MM-RAG systems
Clear problem formulation identifying concrete limitations in existing approaches (expensive MLLM construction and text-centric graphs)
Well-motivated architectural choices combining lightweight rule-based extraction with entity-driven visual grounding to preserve multimodal information
Good reproducibility support with implementation details, hyperparameters per task, dataset preprocessing, and prompts in appendices
Effective qualitative analysis with interpretable case studies demonstrating improvements over baselines
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (dependency parsing, SAM3, EVA-CLIP, Personalized PageRank) without significant methodological innovation

Insufficient analysis of rule-based relation extraction: no quantitative evaluation of precision/recall, no comparison with LLM extraction quality beyond speedup, unclear generalization to diverse domains

Problematic evaluation setup: baseline comparisons use 5k subsets (due to their computational limits) while paper evaluates at larger scales; closed-source models tested on 1k samples only, creating inconsistent comparison scales

Critical missing ablation studies: no ablations on hierarchical structure, rule-based extraction necessity, incidence matrices, graph edge types, or sensitivity to key hyperparameters like grounding threshold τ=0.5

Insufficient visual grounding analysis: grounding threshold appears arbitrary, handling of entities without visual detections unclear, entity names as semantic prompts may fail for abstract entities, no analysis of SAM3 confidence calibration

Limited cross-modal analysis: despite claiming to address 'difficult cross-modal retrieval,' evaluations primarily use single-modality queries with cross-modal evidence rather than true multimodal queries

Significant task-specific hyperparameter sensitivity (Table 5): many parameters vary substantially across datasets, raising concerns about generalization and requiring substantial domain-specific tuning
Incomplete scalability analysis: efficiency measured for construction only, inference-time performance unclear, storage requirements not discussed, scalability to millions of documents not addressed
No failure case analysis or error mode discussion, limiting understanding of method limitations
Potential venue mismatch: primarily a multimodal NLP/systems paper with limited pure computer vision contributions; better suited for EMNLP or ACM MM

strengths: Addresses genuine practical bottleneck: 43.3× speedup and 23.9× cost reduction in graph construction while maintaining or improving downstream performance—highly valuable for deploying MM-RAG systems at scale

Comprehensive experimental validation: four diverse multimodal tasks (retrieval, VQA, reasoning, classification) across multiple datasets with consistent SOTA results and detailed case studies demonstrating clear improvements

Well-motivated technical design: each component addresses specific limitations—rule-based extraction replaces expensive MLLM calls, entity-driven visual grounding prevents modality loss, multi-granularity retrieval enables structured reasoning
Elegant modality-preserving node fusion: incidence matrices (M_OMI, M_SMI) cleanly maintain fine-grained atomic evidence while enabling unified multimodal retrieval—architecturally sound design
Strong empirical results across diverse scenarios: E-VQA (72.0 R@10), InfoSeek (83.8 R@10), ScienceQA (97.85 accuracy), CrisisMMD (61.70)—notably exceeds human performance on ScienceQA
Practical applicability: clear implementation details with extensive appendix documentation enable reproducibility; addresses scalability concerns blocking adoption of graph-based MM-RAG
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (rule-based dependency parsing, SAM visual grounding, Personalized PageRank)—contribution is primarily engineering-focused rather than introducing novel methods

Critical missing ablations: no component-level ablations (construction vs. fusion vs. retrieval); no modality-specific ablations validating claims about preserving atomic evidence; claims about 'preserving fine-grained information' lack quantitative validation

Incomplete efficiency analysis: speedup/cost figures only relative to baselines; missing breakdown of time spent on NER, dependency parsing, visual grounding, PPR; no analysis of graph complexity or whether SAM-3 is the actual bottleneck

Unfair baseline comparisons: knowledge base restricted to 5k for E-VQA/InfoSeek because baselines cannot scale—we never observe baseline performance on full datasets where the method shines; closed-source models evaluated on only 1k samples

Extensive hyperparameter tuning undermines generalization: Table 5 shows highly varied task-specific configurations (damping factor α: 0.15–0.85, weights ωC: 0.05–1.2); no sensitivity analysis provided; unclear how to configure for new domains

Visual grounding fragility unaddressed: reliance on entity name matching with SAM prompts may fail for abstract entities; no statistics on segmentation success rates; confidence threshold τ=0.5 appears arbitrary without justification

Insufficient analysis of failure modes: no discussion of when/why method fails; no error analysis; no exploration of precision-recall trade-offs; unclear handling of entities with multiple visual manifestations or ambiguous visual objects

Missing graph-level analysis: no characterization of incidence matrix sizes (M_OMI, M_SMI) at realistic scales; no analysis of graph sparsity patterns or impact on PPR convergence; percentage of entities successfully grounded unknown

Weak theoretical justification: limited principled explanation for why this combination works; no formal approximation analysis comparing to full triplet extraction; design choices appear somewhat ad-hoc

Generalization concerns: most datasets Wikipedia-derived or academic; CrisisMMD is only truly noisy dataset; evaluation on single noisy domain insufficient to claim real-world applicability across domains

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four multimodal tasks with consistent improvements over strong baselines (VaLiK, mKG-RAG, MMGraphRAG)
Significant practical efficiency gains (43.3× speedup, 23.9× cost reduction) enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings
Well-motivated problem identifying genuine limitations in existing MM-RAG systems (expensive construction, text-centric graphs)
Thorough documentation with detailed hyperparameter configurations, ablation studies, and failure case analysis supporting reproducibility
Effective modality-preserving multimodal node fusion design that maintains fine-grained atomic evidence from both modalities
Strong empirical results across diverse backbones (LLaMA, Qwen, GPT-5.2) demonstrating broad applicability
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: combines established techniques (dependency parsing, SAM3, PPR) without significant methodological innovation; individual components are straightforward applications of existing methods

Inadequate analysis of graph construction quality: no evaluation of relation extraction precision/recall vs. LLM-based methods; missing assessment of whether lightweight rules capture equivalent semantic relations; downstream improvements don't prove graph quality
Unfair baseline comparisons: baselines restricted to 5k dataset subsets while MG²-RAG evaluated on full datasets; fundamentally disadvantages baselines and makes true performance assessment difficult

Extensive task-specific hyperparameter tuning required (Table 7: damping factors 0.15-0.85, node weights varying 2-3×) contradicting claims of robustness; sensitivity analysis provided but breadth of variation raises concerns

Limited visual grounding analysis: no evaluation of grounding accuracy or coverage; relies on entity names alone as SAM3 prompts; failure modes (Figure 8) suggest problems with ambiguous references but no systematic analysis of frequency or patterns
Missing comparisons with related approaches: no discussion of other lightweight graph construction methods, alternative modality fusion strategies, or other entity-driven visual grounding techniques

Unfair evaluation metrics: different improvements across tasks use different metrics; some baseline numbers appear surprisingly low (VaLiK 16.16 vs MG²-RAG 62.88 on E-VQA 5k); cost comparison uses specific cloud provider pricing
Incomplete technical specifications: SAM3 configuration sparse; confidence threshold τ=0.5 unjustified; EVA-CLIP-8B choice unexplained; incidence matrix design rationale missing
